title: India's U-18 Women Equalised in the 54th Minute. China Won the Shootout 3-1. The Asia Cup Final Dream Is Over.
excerpt: Nousheen Naz opened the scoring in the third minute and Kiran Ekka forced the shootout with a late penalty corner. But China converted three shootout attempts to India's one, ending an unbeaten group-stage run.
body:
India's U-18 women's hockey team came within a shootout of the Asia Cup final. They left Kakamigahara, Japan, with a bronze-medal match instead.

In a semifinal that swung between dominance and desperation, India drew 2-2 with China in regulation time on Thursday before losing the shootout 3-1. It was the first defeat of the tournament for a side that had scored 30 goals and conceded just two in the group stage — including a 25-0 demolition of Singapore and wins over Malaysia and South Korea.

## The Early Strike and China's Response

India started with the same attacking intent that had defined their pool matches. Captain Sweety Kujur played a pass from midfield into the circle in just the third minute, and Nousheen Naz — the tournament's top scorer with seven goals against Singapore alone — finished with a strong backhand to give India an early lead.

China, however, were not rattled. They controlled more possession through the middle quarters and equalised in the 24th minute when Li ZeYan punished a defensive lapse with a clinical field goal.

## The Defensive Battle

The second and third quarters belonged to the defences. China earned a penalty corner in the 21st minute, but Indian goalkeeper Mahak Parihar denied Feng Jiaxin's drag flick. Another penalty corner in the 34th minute met the same fate, with India's backline standing firm.

India created chances too, forcing consecutive penalty corners in the 43rd minute, but the Chinese defence absorbed everything. The score remained 1-1 heading into the final quarter.

## Zhang's Rebound and Ekka's Answer

China broke through in the 48th minute. Zhang Yuzheng pounced on a rebound from a penalty corner routine to put her side 2-1 ahead. With twelve minutes remaining and a place in the final slipping away, India needed an answer.

It came in the 54th minute. Kiran Ekka converted a penalty corner to drag the score back to 2-2, sending the match into a shootout and keeping Indian hopes alive for a few more minutes.

## The Shootout That Ended It

In the shootout, China's composure proved decisive. They converted three of their attempts while India managed just one. It was a cruel end to a campaign that had been defined by relentless attacking and defensive solidity.

## What It Means for Indian Hockey

India will now play in the third-place match on Saturday. The men's team, meanwhile, has already reached the final after beating Pakistan 5-3, with Purti Ashish Tani scoring four goals.

For the Indian diaspora watching from abroad, the women's U-18 team represents something significant: a generation of players developed through structured grassroots programs who can compete with Asia's best. Nousheen Naz, Sweety Kujur, and Kiran Ekka are names to remember. They may not have reached the final this time, but their performances in Kakamigahara — 30 goals scored in four matches, and a semifinal decided only on shootout margins — signal a program that is moving in the right direction.

The team's unbeaten run in group play, capped by a 25-0 demolition of Singapore, was among the most dominant displays in the tournament's history. The heartbreak of the shootout does not erase that.
